prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed building fire-safety checks

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
Use a transparent A2 trace paper and mark the walls that fail fire-resistance requirements/stairwell enclosure defects/design defects on the tracing. This paper is then rubbed on top of existing plans, so that the wall layout is transferred from the plan. Assemble a stack of such tracings, one for each story or slab (see example).
3. Trace all walls up until the limit of the building, on an A1 response side of a fresh piece of paper, to capture any continuity of failed fire-resistance requirements (see example).
4. Check all defects. Finally, cross-references may be made with drawings to indicate to designers *why* the designer's fire protection philosophy did not work.

**Note**
Examples given are for demonstration purposes only. Please do not copy any part of these plans into your own plans, as the walls shown on the following pages are not accurate.
